
# Blackhole NoC Stream Sweep

Goal: measure peer-tile L1 unicast throughput with enough data in flight to
avoid the tiny-transfer latency trap.

The harness lives in `microbenching/noc/riscv_noc_stream_sweep.py`.

## Method

- A single NoC packet is limited to `NOC_MAX_BURST_SIZE`, which is 16 KiB on
  Blackhole (`NOC_MAX_BURST_WORDS = 256`, 64-byte NoC words).
- Larger logical transfers are issued as command trains: split the transfer into
  16 KiB chunks, submit all chunks, then do one read flush or write barrier.
- The default stream size is 1 MiB per repeat. Repeats overwrite/re-read the same
  1 MiB peer L1 region so the benchmark can transmit many MiB without needing
  more L1 address space.
- Traffic is same-row peer-tile L1 unicast only. No DRAM writes and no multicast.
- The table subtracts an empty loop with the same command-count shape.

## First Observation

The 16 MiB-per-row sweep reaches roughly `63-64 B/cyc` for peer reads and
`64-65 B/cyc` for peer writes. Logical x distance across row 2 still does not
show a clear slope, so either per-router latency is hidden by the pipeline /
ack path at this transfer size, or logical x distance is not mapping cleanly to
physical router count.

The all-to-one sweep to target core `1,2` measured all 120 program cores on both
NoCs, 240 source/NoC rows total. It was also flat: reads ranged from
`62.055` to `63.960 B/cyc` with average `63.567 B/cyc`; writes ranged from
`63.239` to `64.716 B/cyc` with average `64.533 B/cyc`. This looks like a
single-source injection / command-buffer stream limit, not the aggregate fabric
bandwidth.
